hints.title: Successive Sum Recurrence Obstacle
hints.text: Each Fibonacci number is the sum of the two preceding ones. How can computing the series iteratively from the bottom up avoid redundant recalculations?

hints.title: Two-State Constant Shift Invariant
hints.text: Evaluating F(n) depends strictly on F(n-1) and F(n-2). Retaining only the two most recent values is sufficient.

hints.title: Scalar State Progression Procedure
hints.text: If n <= 1, return n directly. Initialize two scalar registers to 0 and 1. Loop n - 1 times, computing their sum and sliding the window forward. Return the leading register.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: index of the Fibonacci number (0 <= N <= 30)
complexity.notes: Iterates N times with two integer variables.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Naive recursion recalculates the same values leading to O(2^N) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant space registers replace array allocation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling base cases n=0 and n=1 cleanly with O(1) space.
